items.project_definition: A synchronization marker indicating that a mandatory structural layer is verified and subsequent development streams can be executed concurrently.
The base architectural layer comprising shared I/O helpers and core entity logic that must be fully implemented before any feature-specific work.
The primary operational objective that defines a successful outcome for a specific user-centric feature set.
A unique sequential integer assigned to each entry to allow precise targeting for updates or deletions.
The lightweight data-interchange format used for persistent storage in the home directory and for machine-readable output.
The smallest viable set of functional capabilities, specifically restricted to creation and completion of entries.
The logical grouping of implementation steps based on user-centric requirements to ensure modular testability.
The set of external design documents and contracts required before execution of the task list.
The primary documentation file describing system usage and persistence behavior.
The initial project bootstrap phase including skeleton creation and tooling configuration.
The specific implementation step responsible for providing a non-empty response when the stored collection is void.
The verification suite split into unit and integration directories to ensure logic correctness.
The act of assigning a timestamp value to the creation field during entity instantiation.
The specific command operation that purges all entries currently marked as finished from the persistent store.
The command operation used to retrieve and display the entire collection of entries in either human or machine-readable formats.
A high-priority blocking constraint indicating that no subsequent phase may be started until the current layer is fully verified.
